Security and VPC/options for private data
transcript:
Meeting header:
[00:00:00] Avery Chen (Redwood): Thanks everyone for joining, we got about 45 minutes, we'll run through the PoV plan, focus on quality eval and hallucination checks. Recording's on.
[00:00:08] Lisa Moran (NovaHealth): Thanks, appreciate it. We've got a small team here — I'm Lisa, Head of AI, Diego is our CTO, Priya will own the data and prompts, Mark on product.
[00:00:17] Diego Ruiz (NovaHealth): Hi all. Quick ask — we care about clinical safety, so hallucination thresholds are a blocker.
[00:00:22] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Totally understood. We'll propose specific hallucination metrics and a reg-test harness you can run locally or we run in the PoV.
[00:00:30] Priya Singh (NovaHealth): One thing — our prompts vary a lot, we have templated EHR extraction prompts and freeform summarization prompts.
[00:00:36] Avery: Good, that diversity is helpful. Goal for today: agree success criteria, what golden prompts look like, what regression tests to run, and timeline for artifact handoff.
[00:00:45] Mark El(l)ison (NovaHealth): Sorry, Mark here — when you say golden prompts, do you mean the set we hand off or you craft them?
[00:00:52] Samir: Usually a combination. Best practice is customer supplies representative prompts (we call them golden prompts) plus expected outputs / acceptance rules. We help augment and sanitize them.
[00:01:02] Lisa: Ok. Walk me through the scoring approach though — how do you quantify hallucination?
[00:01:07] Samir: We use a multi-axis rubric. Example: accuracy (binary or categorical), hallucination flag (0/1 with severity), format compliance score (0-1), and a final weighted score. For NovaHealth we propose weights: Accuracy 50%, Hallucination 30%, Format/Structure 20%.
[00:01:26] Priya: Can you give an example?
[00:01:28] Samir: Sure. For an EHR extraction prompt: expected output fields = {diagnosis_code, onset_date, free_text_summary}. If model returns extra diagnoses not in record that's a hallucination — that's a fail on that field and contributes to hallucination severity. Format compliance checks ensure date iso format, codes match ICD patterns, etc.
[00:01:47] Diego: And regression tests? We want to avoid regressions when you tune quant or swap models.
[00:01:52] Samir: The reg-test harness pins the golden prompt set and runs nightly or per-deploy checks; we compare field-level F1 scores and hallucination rate delta. Any drop beyond the agreed delta triggers an alert. We'll provide a regression CSV with baseline metrics and thresholds.
[00:02:05] Avery: Note — we also include a fallback policy in the PoV: if hallucination rate > X or latency > Y we automatic fallback to a smaller model or to a safe template.
[00:02:13] Lisa: What's realistic for latency? Our SLAs are 500ms p95 per request for short extraction tasks.
[00:02:19] Samir: With Hosted Redwood using a small quantized 7B we typically see 200-400ms p95 depending on sequence length. For long summarize tasks p95 will be higher. We'll capture per-prompt distribution.
[00:02:29] Mark: Are you going to provide throughput forecasts?
[00:02:31] Samir: Yes — we need your QPS profile. If you expect bursts of 200 concurrent, we recommend Dedicated for predictable throughput. For PoV we can emulate burst load with synthetic runner.
[00:02:40] Priya: QPS is low right now — usually 5–20 qps but some nightly batch jobs up to 300 qps for summaries.
[00:02:46] Diego: Security — talk through data residency and encryption.
[00:02:49] Rosa (Redwood CSM): We will send SOC2 docs and our security appendix. For PoV data we advise an anonymized export. If you need VPC/private deployment we'll scope that in parallel — private deployment timeline is longer.
[00:03:02] Lisa: We're leaning to hosted PoV but need assurance on logs and KMS.
[00:03:06] Samir: We support customer KMS for private keys but the hosted PoV can use envelope encryption; audit logs are exportable. We'll note that in the security appendix.
[00:03:15] Mark: Back to eval — what does a golden prompt look like?
[00:03:18] Samir: Each golden prompt should include: the prompt text, input record id (pseudonymized), expected output or schema, a short rationale and severity tags (safety, format, critical). We'll ask for about 5,000 prompts across templates split by workload type: extraction (50%), summarization (30%), reranking (20%).
[00:03:36] Lisa: 5k is a lot — can we start smaller?
[00:03:39] Avery: For PoV we usually accept a minimum of 500 high-quality golden prompts + 500 samples for hallucination probing. That said, more prompts gives higher statistical confidence.
[00:03:50] Priya: We'll try for 5k but will at least provide 1k to start.
[00:03:54] Samir: Great. On hallucination probes: we create negative-control prompts (inputs missing the answer) and check if model fabricates values. These get a high severity tag. We'll return ROC-style curves showing false-positive hallucination rate vs threshold.
[00:04:08] Diego: How do you handle partial matches? Like model returns approximate dates?
[00:04:12] Samir: Our scoring allows fuzzy matches with configurable tolerances for specific fields (e.g., dates within 2 days, numeric within ±5%). We mark exact match vs fuzzy and adjust weights.
[00:04:23] Mark: Can the regression harness be dockerized and run in our infra?
[00:04:26] Samir: Yes, we provide a runner that can run locally or in your VPC in PoV. For hosted we host the runner and publish results to the console.
[00:04:35] Lisa: What about hallucination categories — factual vs fabricated clinical statements?
[00:04:39] Samir: We'll annotate hallucinations into categories: fabricated facts, extraneous clinical assertions, hallucinated citations, and incorrect numeric data. Different severity. Clinical fabrications will be treated as high severity with lower tolerated rate.
[00:04:52] Priya: Any recommended tooling for annotation?
[00:04:55] Samir: We often recommend a lightweight CSV with columns (prompt_id, expected, actual, hallucination_flag, hallucination_type, severity, notes). For larger efforts Redwood can ingest annotated results and produce dashboards.
[00:05:07] Lisa: Can you also show sample dashboards?
[00:05:09] Rosa: We'll attach a dashboard screenshot and a sample PoV dashboard link in the follow-up email.
[00:05:15] Mark: On scoring — is there a binary pass/fail or continuous score?
[00:05:19] Samir: Both. Each prompt gets a continuous score. We set a pass/fail threshold (e.g., mean weighted score >= 0.85 and hallucination rate <= 1%). We recommend the threshold be negotiated per workload.
[00:05:32] Lisa: Ok, timeline?
[00:05:34] Avery: Proposed PoV schedule: Week 0 (this week): artifact handoff and runbook. Week 1: baseline runs and initial scoring. Week 2: parameter tuning, quantization tests, hallucination probes and regression run. Check-in end of week 2. Decision at end of week 3.
[00:05:48] Priya: Does Week 2 include a model variant test (e.g., 7B quantized vs 13B fp16)?
[00:05:52] Samir: Yes, we'll compare 7B quantized, 13B int8 (if available) and a safety-tuned variant. We'll capture latency and cost per 1,000 tokens and per-record.
[00:06:02] Diego: Who's responsible for the scoring script?
[00:06:04] Samir: Redwood provides the scoring harness; we'll publish as a python package and a docker image. You can run it locally.
[00:06:11] Mark: Any red flags we should be aware of?
[00:06:13] Samir: Biggest risk is low-quality golden prompts — they'll bias the evaluation. Also insufficient negative controls can under-detect hallucination. We'll give annotation guidance.
[00:06:23] Lisa: How will we measure cost? Per-token only?
[00:06:26] Samir: We'll provide cost per 1k tokens and cost-per-request for your canonical prompts. Redwood Console will break down token types and KV cache hits. For PoV we'll estimate cost using run traces.
[00:06:36] Priya: Do you support prefix caching for repeated patient history prompts?
[00:06:39] Samir: Yes, caching and KV-cache mention — sorry the recorder might write KV cup or something, it's KV cache. It can reduce cost significantly for repeated context. We'll include caching scenarios in the benchmark.
[00:06:51] Lisa: Good. Anything else on compliance?
[00:06:53] Rosa: We'll include the audit log export process and retention policies. If you need HIPAA-specific language we can loop in security team.
[00:07:02] Diego: Let's talk acceptance criteria concretely.
[00:07:05] Samir: Proposal (example): 1) Mean weighted score across golden prompts >= 0.85. 2) Hallucination rate (any high-severity hallucination) <= 0.5%. 3) Format compliance >= 95% (dates/codes/required fields). 4) Latency p95 <= 500ms for extraction templates and p95 <= 1.5s for summarization. 5) Cost-per-1k-tokens aligned to target (we'll quantify). If any of these fail the PoV returns recommendations or a canary fallback.
[00:07:31] Priya: Those look reasonable. We'll try to tighten hallucination to <=0.25% for critical clinical prompts.
[00:07:36] Lisa: Okay that works.
[00:07:38] Avery: Recap — I'll send the runbook, Rosa will send the security appendix and dashboard screenshots. Priya will share prompts and samples by next Wednesday. Samir will run baseline sweep and share latency/cost and scoring harness. We'll meet 2025-11-26 for the week-2 review.
[00:07:55] Mark: Perfect.
[00:07:58] Lisa: Thanks everyone.
[00:08:00] Avery: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and owners.
